_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 8: VLT MOONS (id 'moons')
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote; DERIVED = arithmetic done here; EFFECTIVE = chosen to reproduce published performance; INFERRED = a reading not stated; MEASURED = read from a figure with a stated scale; NOT FOUND = gap.
_meta.status: commissioning; first observations summer 2026 (P26); ESO page 'AIV -> Commissioning' (E26): mark presets '(design)'

C20.cite: Cirasuolo, M., Fairley, A., Rees, P., et al. 2020, The Messenger 180, 10, "MOONS: The New Multi-Object Spectrograph for the VLT", arXiv:2009.00628 (ADS 2020Msngr.180...10C; open access). Overview: Table 1 key parameters, Fig. 2 hardware, Fig. 3 R(lambda)

O16.cite: Oliva, E., Delabre, B., Tozzi, A., et al. 2016, Proc. SPIE 9908, 99087R, "Toward the final optical design of MOONS, the Multi-Object Optical and Near-Infrared spectrograph for the VLT" (ADS 2016SPIE.9908E..7RO; author copy from the Cambridge repository; the PDF is the SPIE-formatted text). The final-design spectrograph: Table 1, Fig. 1 (layout, LR and HR), Table 2, Fig. 2, 3

O14.cite: Oliva, E., Todd, S., Cirasuolo, M., et al. 2014, Proc. SPIE 9147, 91472C, "Updated optical design and trade-off study for MOONS, the Multi-Object Optical and Near Infrared spectrometer for the VLT", arXiv:1407.3054 (ADS 2014SPIE.9147E..2CO). Pre-PDR trade-off: on-axis collimator, dichroic cuts, VPH-plus-prism dispersers, Table 1, 2, Fig. 1, 2, 7

F22.cite: Fisher, M., Black, M., King, D., et al. 2022, Proc. SPIE 12184, 121846W, "Optical performance and results from the alignment and testing of the cameras for the MOONS spectrograph" (ADS 2022SPIE12184E..6WF; STFC repository copy STFC-APV-2023-018). As-built cameras: Table 1, Figs. 1-3, Sec. 2-3, 6

G22.cite: Gonzalez, O., Cirasuolo, M., Taylor, W., et al. 2022, Proc. SPIE 12184, 1218412, "MOONS - Multi Object spectroscopy for the VLT: overview and instrument integration update" (ADS 2022SPIE12184E..12G; STFC repository copy STFC-APV-2023-029). Sec. 2.1 overview, Fig. 1 (hardware), Fig. 3 (layout)

C12.cite: Cirasuolo, M., Afonso, J., Bender, R., et al. 2012, Proc. SPIE 8446, 84460S, "MOONS: a Multi-Object Optical and Near-infrared Spectrograph for the VLT", arXiv:1208.5780 (ADS 2012SPIE.8446E..0SC). Phase-A concept: the fiber sub-system (Sec. 4.3)

GU22.cite: Guinouard, I., Laporte, P., Amans, J.-P., et al. 2022, Proc. SPIE 12188, 121885S, "MOONS - Multi Object Spectroscopy for the VLT: Final performances and integration of the fibres" (ADS 2022SPIE12188E..5SG; 12 pp.; the fiber link: Sec. 2 performances, Sec. 3.2 slit alignment, Figs. 1, 2, 5)

params.value: spherical mirror
params.quote: collimated using a spherical mirror and fed via two dichroics to three dispersing elements and three cameras

params.value: ON-AXIS: the slit stands in the collimated beam (trade-off baseline); colTilt 0
params.quote: The collimator consists of a single spherical mirror working on-axis. The input slit is positioned at the focus of the mirror.
params.alt: O14 Sec. 3: "The main drawback is the obscuration the collimated beam by the input slit. However, with a careful mechanical design, the fraction of vignetted beam can be limited to ~1.9%." Table 3: "Input slits obscures ~1.9% of the collimated beam". Final design (O16 Fig. 1, F22) keeps the spherical collimator; O16 Fig. 1 draws the slit mark inside the returning beam (MEASURED, see Layout)

params.quote: Focal ratio collimator FCOLL = 3.50 ... Diameter of collimated beam DCOLL = 265 mm

params.quote: Diameter of collimated beam DCOLL = 265 mm

params.value: two dichroics in the collimated beam: three arms RI, YJ, H
params.quote: The collimated beam is split into the three arms by two dichroic beam-splitters.

params.value: 0.95 um (RI | YJ); 1.40 um (YJ | H)
params.quote: The longest wavelengths (λ>1.4 µm) are reflected by the first dichroic toward the H arm. The shortest wavelengths ((λ<0.95 µm) are reflected by the second dichroic toward the RI arm. The remaining light (0.95 µm <λ<1.40 µm) passes through the second dichroic and feeds the YJ arm.
params.alt: Cuts chosen in regions of bad telluric transmission (O14 Sec. 6). The final design reverses the order (see Layout); the 2016 and later papers give only the arm bands, so the cuts are carried over (INFERRED) and agree with the bands 934-955 nm overlap and the 1350-1452 nm gap

params.parameter: Dichroic order in the final design
params.value: first Dichroic I (reflects RI), then Dichroic H (reflects YJ, transmits H): INFERRED from ray colors in O16 Fig. 1
params.alt: O14 Sec. 6 had H reflected first and said the layout was not ideal for the coatings: "it transmits short and reflects longer wavelengths". O16 Fig. 1 shows the RI beam leaving at the first plate and the red passing the second plate straight to GRT-H

params.value: VPH transmission gratings; YJ one fixed grating; RI and H each interchange a low- and a high-resolution disperser (VPH plus prisms)
params.quote: The YJ arm is equipped with a fixed transmission grating that disperses the light. The RI and H arms include interchangeable dispersive systems made by a combination of transmission gratings and prisms.

params.value: 5 per spectrograph (3 low-resolution, 2 high-resolution)
params.quote: Each of the two MOONS spectrographs has five highly efficient volume phase holographic (VPH) dispersers, three for the low-resolution mode and two for the high-resolution mode.

params.value: one linear mechanism through the bench swaps the RI (and the H) disperser between modes
params.quote: using a single common linear mechanism that passes straight through the optical bench

params.value: 4 deg (against ghosts)
params.quote: the gratings work with an off-axis angle of 4 degrees, relative to the Littrow configuration

params.value: i-VPH (prisms glued to the grating) for RI; p-VPH or i/p-VPH with mono-crystalline silicon prisms for YJ and H high-dispersion
params.quote: Such dynamic ranges can only be achieved using p-VPHs with prisms of mono-crystalline Silicon
params.alt: O14 Sec. 5: "In the RI arm, the change of resolving between MR and HR configurations is a factor of two (see Table 2). This can be achieved using two i-VPH’s with opposite angles directions". The final design (O16 Fig. 1) draws P-HR-I, P-HR-H prisms beside GRT-HR-I and GRT-HR-H; prism glass and apex angles NOT FOUND

params.value: transparency of Si prisms at short wavelengths depends on temperature
params.quote: The internal transmission of Silicon at these short wavelengths depends strongly on the temperature.

params.alt: FITTED with web/physics.js (read-only; gType trans, tAlpha = incidence, core 158 um, F 3.5, D 8.0, W 265, fcam 251.75, 4096 x 15 um, lamC = band midpoint 1581.5 nm) so that R = 18800 (design table) and the dispersion = band width / 4096 px (DERIVED target) both hold; two parameters, two targets, so this is a fit not a test. No VPH line density, angle or prism is published in Black 2022 or the other accessible papers. Published 1056 /mm at AOI 53 deg (FJ25): with 1056 at 53.0 the model gives R 18795 and 0.277 A/px.

layout.text: O16 Fig. 1 (PDF p. 3), top panel: LR configuration; bottom panel: HR configuration; plan view with a 1 m scale bar. Also G22 Fig. 3 (p. 4, same drawing, not measured), F22 Figs. 1-2 (p. 2-3), O14 Fig. 1 (p. 3).

Fiber slit (a small mark inside the beam) -> spherical collimator at the far (right) end -> beam returns past the slit mark -> Dichroic I -> Dichroic H -> arms. Collimator vertex to slit mark 457 px = 0.99 m (460 px = 1 m) -> f_col about 0.93 m (927.5 mm sourced by DERIVED).

O14 Sec. 3 ON-AXIS trade-off baseline (quote above); the slit mark lies in the collimated beam in O16 Fig. 1 (both panels), between the mirror and Dichroic I. VERDICT: ON-AXIS, colTilt 0, the slit obscures about 1.9% of the beam (O14 Table 3). Caution: O14 compared three collimators; O16, F22 and G22 say only 'spherical mirror' and keep the same figure geometry. F22 Sec. 6 notes a test bench with 'the second of the two MOONS collimator mirrors' (one mirror per spectrograph, two in all).
Plate at about 0.64 of the collimator-to-grating path (570 of 893 px); reflects the RI beam by 120 deg (AOI about 28 deg), transmits the rest. Ray colors: blue leaves here.

Plate at about 0.82 of the path (720 of 881 px); reflects the YJ beam by about 107 deg (AOI about 37 deg), transmits the red (H) beam straight on. The figure labels are 'Dichroic I' and 'Dichroic H'; which beam each plate reflects is INFERRED from the ray colors (the 2014 design had H reflected first: O14 Sec. 6).

Collimator to GRT-RI about 893 px = 1.94 m, to GRT-YJ 881 px = 1.92 m, to GRT-H 890 px = 1.93 m (path through the dichroic centers). 2 f_col = 1.855 m (the pupil at the center of curvature, as for an on-axis spherical collimator); the figure's 1.93 m is 4% longer. Preset layLen 1930 (MEASURED) with 1855 as the alternative.

Each grating is a plate in the collimated beam just after its dichroic. LR: GRT-RI, GRT-YJ, GRT-H alone. HR: the RI beam crosses P-HR-I, GRT-HR-I, P-HR-I (two prisms flanking the grating; the figure labels two P-HR-I plates and GRT-HR-I), the H beam crosses P-HR-H, GRT-HR-H, P-HR-H; YJ unchanged (GRT-YJ). In the model each is an equivalent single transmission grating.

Each camera stands about 0.34-0.42 m beyond its grating (grating to the first lens L1: RI 169 px = 0.37 m, YJ 155 px = 0.34 m, H 195 px = 0.42 m). Camera axes in the 2016 drawing: RI 10 deg to the right of YJ, H 22 deg to the left of YJ (the grating plates are placed about +-8 deg off those axes). As built (F22 Sec. 3): optical axes at 98, 76.4 and 52 deg to gravity (RI, YJ, H): 21.6 deg and 24.4 deg apart, the RI-YJ separation larger than the 2016 drawing. All three cameras identical in form (mirror and corrector lens pair, detector inside L1), mirror at the far end, detector at the back focus near the grating side.

O16 Table 2: length 430 mm, largest lens 400 mm, mirror 440 mm, central obscuration 19%; F22 Sec. 2.2: L1 is a meniscus with a central rectangular aperture holding L2 and the detector package. Explorer cam 'mirror' (catadioptric, internal focus).

performance_targets.src: F22 Table 1; measured 2.5-2.7 px FWHM in RI and YJ (F22 summary)

not_found: Line density, incidence and diffraction angles, substrate, prism glass and apex angles and the cryogenic index source for the five VPH dispersers: not in Black 2022 or Guinouard 2020 (only HR-H 1056 /mm at AOI 53 deg, secondary FJ25). The explorer gratings are EFFECTIVE, fitted to R and dispersion.

Dichroic transition widths, final cut wavelengths and angles of incidence (Black 2022 has no layout figure with dimensions; Fig. 4 shows the fixed-optics assembly photo/CAD only); dichroic substrate and thickness.

As-built fiber core diameter (Guinouard 2022, the fiber-link paper, gives no core diameter or on-sky size; it confirms the f/3.65 microlens input and an f/3.5 output test). Measured FRD value: only the transmission including FRD is given (75.3%). Fiber pitch within a slitlet, slitlet pitch and the gaps between slitlets: not published (only the 200 mm length and 512 fibers).
Measured R(lambda) as numbers and dispersion in A/px: BL22 gives only Fig. 11 (YJ R(lambda) plot, expected center 4000) and the statement that R~4000 is met; HR measurements were pending.
Throughput numbers by arm: C20 Table 1 quotes only '> 30% in low resolution, > 25% in high resolution' (total instrument), Fig. 3 plots.

Source: the SPIE papers by Black et al. 2022 (spectrograph performance), Guinouard et al. 2022 (fibers), Taylor et al. 2018 are not openly available (SPIE paywall; the INAF and HAL copies sit behind bot checks and were not fetched).
Which of the two slit radii (1110 mm, 900 mm) is the spatial curvature.
Collimator mirror radius (center of curvature) and the off-axis offset of the slit: not given.
conflicts: Fiber on-sky size, RESOLVED as far as the documents allow (INFERRED): 1.0 arcsec (O16 design; GU20 abstract 'sub field of 1 arcsec'; GU20 requirement '>= 1 arcsec') versus 1.2 arcsec (C20 Table 1, G22 Sec. 2.1, the built instrument). Core: 158 um as built (GU20) against 150 um in the design. The built core is 5% larger than the design and 1.2/1.0 = 20% larger on the sky only if the field stop was enlarged too, so the later 1.2 arcsec is taken as the built aperture; the fiber core in the explorer now follows GU20. Older text: Fiber on-sky size: 1.0 arcsec (O16 Table 1, E26 baseline table; design) vs 1.2 arcsec (C20 Table 1; G22 Sec. 2.1; built). The core is 150 um in the design (O14, O16, F22 test fibers) and 140-170 um for 1-1.2 arcsec in phase A (C12); the as-built core is NOT FOUND. Recommended: enter 150 um at f/3.5 (virtual, 1.105 arcsec) and note both.

Resolving powers: O16/F22 Table 1: LR RI 4500, YJ 4300, H 6800; HR RI 9100, H 18800. C20 Table 1: LR RI 4100, YJ 4300, H 6600; HR RI 9200, H 19700. E26: LR RI 4100, H 6600; HR-I 9200, HR-H 18300. G22: 'R~4000-7500' LR, 'R~9000, 4000, 19700' HR. The later (built) numbers are lower in RI-LR and H-LR and higher in HR-H. Recommended validation targets: the C20 values, as the most recent public table.
HR-H band: O16 1523-1640 nm; C20 1.52-1.64 um; E26 1.521-1.641 um (same band within 1 nm).

Dichroic order and sense: O14 (2014): first dichroic reflects H (>1.4 um), second reflects RI (<0.95 um), YJ transmitted. O16 Fig. 1 (2016): Dichroic I first (RI reflected), Dichroic H second (YJ reflected, H transmitted) INFERRED from ray colors. O14 itself says the 2014 order was not ideal for the coatings.

Collimator geometry: BL22 Sec. 2 says the collimator is below the slit and returns the beam 'back up over the slit'. It does not contradict the on-axis reading but does not confirm the 1.9% obscuration either; the verdict stays ON-AXIS (colTilt 0) with this flag.

Slit curvature: O14 Fig. 2 (2014 design) R = 940 mm cylinder with a second curvature in the other plane; GU22 Sec. 3.2 (as built) two perpendicular arcs of 1110 mm and 900 mm. 940 mm lies between the two; the later pair is adopted for drawing, pending which plane each is in.
Camera angles: the 2016 drawing has the RI camera 10 deg from YJ; F22 (as built) 21.6 deg from YJ.
Temperature: C20 -130 C; F22 'approximately 128 K' (= -145 C); P26 -143 to -233 C. Different elements.

Collimator type: O14 Sec. 3 (trade-off) names on-axis, RFL-Schmidt and Maksutov options; only O14 states 'on-axis'. The later papers say 'a spherical mirror' (F22, O16, G22) and G22's text says 'collimator sits at the base of the optical bench'. An older phase-A summary says on-axis parabola (not saved).
notes: Status: MOONS had its first light on the VLT in summer 2026 (ESO announcement 3 September 2026, P26); the ESO project page of 2026-11-17 still reads 'AIV -> Commissioning' (E26). It is not yet in science operation, so the preset name carries '(design)'. Recommended text: 'design values from the 2016-2022 papers; first light 3 Sep 2026, commissioning'.

Telescope pupil: the explorer's VLT convention is Nasmyth 8000 mm at f/15 (UVES, MUSE; VLT-SPE-ESO-10000-2723). MOONS is on UT1 Nasmyth A (G22); its microlens converts f/15 to f/3.65 (C12). The telescope enters only through D = 8.0 m and the virtual F = 3.5 (core / (F x D)).

Fibers (priority 1, Guinouard 2022): f/3.65 microlens input and f/3.5 output are confirmed, so the virtual F = 3.5 stands. (Superseded by GU20: core 158 um.) Earlier: 150 um / (3.5 x 8000 mm) x 206264.806 = 1.105 arcsec; x sqrt(3)/2 = 0.957. If the built fibers were 1.2 arcsec with f/3.65 at f/15 on the 8.0 m pupil, the core would be 1.2 arcsec x 0.5818 mm/arcsec / (15/3.65) = 0.170 mm (DERIVED from the phase-A 140-170 um range of C12); then the virtual angle = 0.170/(3.5 x 8000) = 1.252 arcsec and the slit 1.084 arcsec. No document settles it, so the 150 um design value is kept and the alternative is recorded.

Pseudo-slit fgroups (priority 2): [16, 108, 108] um on the detector (INFERRED: 16 fibers per slitlet at the sourced 7.2 px pitch, no gap because the slitlet gap is NOT FOUND); on the slit the same group is [16, 398, 398] um (108 / 0.2714). Slit length 200 mm / 512 = 0.391 mm mean pitch, so the gaps are at most a fraction of a pitch.

Virtual convention with the AS-BUILT core (GU20 158 um): 158 um / (3.5 x 8000 mm) x 206264.806 = 1.164 arcsec full width; x sqrt(3)/2 = 1.008 arcsec equal-line-width slit (was 0.957 with 150 um). The sky-equivalent 1.2 arcsec needs D = 0.158/(3.5 x 1.2 x 4.848e-6) = 7.76 m, 3% under 8.0 m (the f/3.65 vs f/3.5 conversion is 4%). Slit image 0.158 x 0.2714 = 42.9 um = 2.86 px at the center against the measured 2.5-2.7 px FWHM (Black 2022) and the 2.7 px design. Older note: core 150 um / (3.5 x 8000 mm) = 1.105 arcsec (the on-sky design size is 1.0 arcsec for an effective 8.8 m aperture with eta_FRD = 0.90, O16); the equal-line-width slit is 0.957 arcsec. Slit image 0.150 x 0.95/3.5 = 40.7 um = 2.71 px (sourced Nres 2.7).

Measured performance (BL22): YJ image 2.5 px FWHM at the center to 2.7 at the corners; RI 2.5 to 3 px; resolving power requirement met (R~4000 in YJ; no numbers in the text; Fig. 11 plot not digitized); all 512 spectra seen, dark gaps between spectra. HR dispersers and the H arm were not yet tested. Throughput: fiber link 69.3% (GU20) / about 69% (GU22); front-end fibers 93.6% / 94.1%; slit-end bundles 76.7% (first slit) / 75.3% (all 64); FRD throughput F/3.65 -> F/3.5: 89.7% warm, 90.1% at 140 K (GU20).
Dispersion (DERIVED from the band edges, 4096 px): RI LR 0.752, YJ 1.016, H LR 0.850, RI HR 0.322, H HR 0.286 A/px. These ignore chip-edge losses; they are not published values.

The explorer cannot represent: the five exchangeable VPH-plus-prism dispersers as such (each is an equivalent single transmission grating), the curved slit with its second curvature, the camera's 19% central obscuration, and cryogenic silicon prisms. The HR RI and H dispersers differ in R and band only through G and tAlpha here.

Two Preset-menu lines recommended: 'MOONS (LR)' with settings RI / YJ / H and 'MOONS (HR)' with settings RI / YJ / H (YJ is identical in both modes), so that the All-arms view for each mode has its own tree (keys 'MOONS LR' and 'MOONS HR').
Layout measurements were made on a 300 dpi render of O16 Fig. 1 page 3 (crop x 500, y 750, 1900 x 1250 px); the scale bar spans 78 to 538 px (460 px = 1 m). Angles are +-4 deg; distances +-5%.
